correctness.rationale: Newton recurrence gives the total ordinary degree d=(n-1)/2, infinity support P and Q, and the rational quotient map. The affine locus is the smooth finite quotient of a smooth curve in characteristic zero. e1=0 meets Fermat transversely away from the two triple-cycle points; these have intersection multiplicity 1 (n=6l+5) or 2 (n=6l+1). Generic S3 orbits give smooth branches b=lambda a^3+... with pairwise different lambda=e3^2/e2^3, so contact order exactly three. At the order-three stabilizer the nonstandard local power-sum expansions give smooth distinguished branches b=a/(l+1)+... or b=-l a^2+..., yielding contacts 1 or 2. This exhausts normalization preimages; delta and Milnor follow from smooth branch contacts; known genus gives an independent defect cross-check. Exact symbolic checker independently ran and passed for n=5,7,11,13,17,19,23,25,29,31; first two outside scope. Checks are not substituted for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary article supplies the affine Newton-sum model and genus of the smooth Fermat quotient, but not the boundary singularity and its complete tangency/contact classification for the ordinary plane projective closure. Neither degree nor genus alone implies the pairwise intersection spectrum, number of branches or mod-six distinguished-branch transition. Searches in published published-finding corpus and accessible primary/web literature did not identify a stronger covering theorem. This is qualified by unindexed literature and a different earlier degree-eleven quotient plane model and possible unindexed sources.
residual_risks: Unindexed classical accounts of Newton power-sum plane models might prove an equivalent all-degree boundary-contact theorem; available searches do not certify priority.
Tzermias (2003) supplies a different singular projective model for n=11, so the distinction between models is essential to the scope and novelty comparison.
Same-model scientific review is not independent formal certification or a publication-priority guarantee.

value.rationale: The starting work uses an explicit two-coordinate plane equation for high-genus symmetric Fermat quotients. Knowing its entire ordinary projective boundary singularity (unique support, smooth branches, contact graph, delta and Milnor, and mod-six transition) is geometrically natural and strictly finer than the known genus. It permits explicit normalization/conductor and local plane-curve calculations for every admissible n. It is neither a mere reparametrization nor a small finite computation.
